Verified the fix: zero pageerrors and zero occurrences of 'destroy is not a function' across (a) voice mode full 3-question flow with typed answers, (b) voice-stop flow with 1 answer, and (c) text mode with 2 answers. All iv-evaluation blocks render as expected and iv-report renders in every flow. critical_code_review_comments: Fix applied in InterviewChat.js (line 24-26) and VoiceTranscript.js (line 7-9) is correct: useEffect callbacks are now wrapped in braces so they return undefined instead of the Promise returned by element.scrollIntoView() in newer Chrome. Consider adding an ESLint rule (consistent-return / react-hooks/exhaustive-deps with --no-implicit-return hint) or a short code review guideline to flag single-expression effect callbacks that call DOM APIs, to prevent regressions elsewhere.
AutoSubmit.js is clean and small; the 10s option simply added to OPTIONS array works end-to-end. No concerns.

rca of the issue: RCA: In React 18+, useEffect's callback body `end.current?.scrollIntoView(...)` was an implicit arrow return. In newer Chromium builds, scrollIntoView() returns a Promise, which React then treated as the effect's cleanup function. On the next effect re-run, React invokes `destroy()` → 'TypeError: destroy is not a function' (safelyCallDestroy / commitHookEffectListUnmount). Reproduction: trigger a state update that re-runs the effect (e.g. answering a question updates msgs/log, triggering the scroll effect). Mitigation: wrap in braces so the callback returns undefined — applied in InterviewChat.js and VoiceTranscript.js. Verified in this iteration with 0 destroy errors across voice 3Q, voice-stop, and text flows.
